This is a brutal spot for Leavitt, and I would even take the Volunteers to win outright . Jim Knowles has worked his magic with Tennessee's defense, and it's second nationally in sacks (39) and third in havoc rate (22.7%). It's one of the most disruptive defenses in the country, and Leavitt has been at his worst against LSU's top opponents. Tennessee ranks top 10 nationally in EPA per play , available yards percentage (32.8%), early-down EPA per play, and third/fourth down success rate (33.6%). LSU's is just as impressive, though; it ranks No. 1 nationally in sacks (40) and No. 4 in havoc rate (22.2%). That spells trouble for Vols QB George MacIntyre . With MacIntyre at the helm, Tennessee is 116th in pass success rate (38.7%). LSU vs Tennessee combo This game will be beautiful if you love defense. Both defenses are ranked in the top 10 by SP+, and they've dominated opponents with their pass rushes this season. No team has more sacks than LSU and Tennessee, and neither program has a QB capable of handling pressure. This might end up being a race to 20 points, if we even get there. Tennessee has the edge, though, with how mistake-prone Leavitt is in big games and how well the Volunteers have played at home this season. Tennessee is 3-0 ATS vs. Top 25 teams at home, and while LSU isn't ranked, it might as well be since the Tigers are the favorite. Neyland Stadium's home-field advantage is real, and with a half dozen future NFL players on its defense, the Vols are allowing just 12.5 points per game at home in conference play . Projected first-round defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam (34 pressures, 6 sacks) will be especially difficult for LSU to handle, but it's really Knowles' exotic blitzes that will really be a problem for a sporadic QB like Leavitt. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:59 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Any thought that LSU was going to take the college football world by storm after Lane Kiffin took over ended with a tough 22-21 loss against Texas. It was the Tigers' fourth loss of the season, they're out of the College Football Playoff mix, and now it's time to play the spoiler role. Kiffin gets to play the villain, going back to his old coaching grounds – he was the Tennessee head coach in 2009 – and Tennessee will be fired up. The Vols are 8-2 after winning five of their last six games, and at No. 9 in the latest rankings, they're all but in the CFP if they win their last two games. LSU vs Tennessee: Quick Hits LSU closes out on the road at Arkansas after this. Lose to the Vols, and it'll be the third year in a row the program suffered a three-game losing streak. Tennessee goes to Vanderbilt to finish up the regular season. If it wins the final two games, it's in the mix for the SEC Championship along with the CFP. The two programs haven't met since 2022 – a 40-13 Tennessee win. LSU has won five of the last six, going back to 2005. How To Watch LSU vs Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why LSU Will Win The talent is still there, the coaching is still great, and now the pressure is off. LSU isn't going anywhere this season, and now it can be Lane Unleashed as the team throws everything at a Vols team with all of the weight on its side of the field. The defense is the best in the SEC, the offense is the best in the SEC, the team holds the ball longer than anyone else in the conference, and no one in America generates more sacks. Tennessee has a problem keeping defenses out of the backfield, and now, here come the Tigers. Why Tennessee Will Win LSU might generate the most sacks in America, but Tennessee can bring the heat, too – the Tigers are No. 2 in sacks. It didn't sack Marcel Reed in last week's 22-7 win over Texas A&M, but it gave him a rough time. Now the Vols are back at home, where they take their defensive production up several notches. The defense has allowed just one touchdown pass in five games in Neyland, but in this, it's about the Tennessee run defense. LSU is 1-3 when running for fewer than 140 yards. Auburn and Furman – the Vols called off the dogs against the Paladins – are the only teams to hit the 140-yard mark. LSU vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines Here's the thing about LSU this season. It pounces on the weak, but its best win is … at Auburn? That's good, but there really isn't a second-best victory going 0-4 against the current CFP-ranked teams on the slate. Tennessee is a top team. This might not be the sexiest team going, but it's got grit. It's a tough defensive team that doesn't make a ton of mistakes, and it doesn't get rattled. LSU will be terrific, but like the Kentucky and Texas games, it'll crumble late in the final moments. Mike Ianniello · Action Network Sat, November 21, 2026 at 7:24 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The LSU Tigers take on the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday, Nov. 21. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. LSU is favored by 1.5 points (-104) on the spread with a moneyline of -110. Tennessee enters as a 1.5-point (-116) underdog and is -110 on the moneyline. The over/under sits at 45.5 total points (-110 / -110). Here's my LSU vs. Tennessee prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 21. LSU vs. Tennessee Pick: Tennessee ML (Play to -110) My Tennessee vs. LSU best bet is on the Volunteers to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . LSU vs Tennessee Odds, Betting Lines LSU vs Tennessee Spread : LSU -1.5, Tennessee +1.5 LSU vs Tennessee Over/Under : 45.5 Points LSU vs Tennessee Moneyline : LSU ML -113, Tennessee ML -108 For a school that expects to be competing for National Championships every season, LSU's first year under Lane Kiffin has not gone as planned. A last-minute loss to Texas last week dropped the Tigers to 6-4 and knocked them out of the College Football Playoff. Now, the challenge for Kiffin will be getting his team off the mat and up for a game against his former team. Things have been up-and-down for transfer quarterback Sam Leavitt in Baton Rouge. The Tigers have gotten the good with the bad. Leavitt leads the SEC in completions and passing yards this season, but he also leads the conference with 12 interceptions. Leavitt is incredibly dynamic with his legs, scoring eight touchdowns on the ground and creating a dangerous running attack with Dilin Jones. We know a Kiffin offense is going to have explosive wideouts, led by the dynamic Jackson Harris on the outside. The offense has been efficient, ranking sixth in the country in Success Rate, but the turnovers and red-zone woes have killed them. When things are clicking, the offense looks great. They have just failed to come up big when needed. Defensive coordinator Blake Baker has fielded LSU's best defense in a while. This unit ranks 11th in Success Rate allowed and has been a force at creating Havoc. Defensive linemen Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross have been a force getting into the backfield and a big reason why the Tigers lead the nation in sacks. The secondary is also terrific, led by cornerbacks DJ Pickett and PJ Woodland, as well as safety Ty Benefield. The group has led the Tigers to a top-10 passing defense. LSU has allowed just eight passing touchdowns all season and has tallied 12 interceptions. With two games to go, Tennessee is on the verge of reaching the College Football Playoff for the second time in three years and is ranked in the top 10. It's Senior Night in Neyland, and old rival Kiffin is in town, so you know this crowd will be fired up. Despite the team's success, it certainly hasn't been the offense pulling the sleigh for head coach Josh Heupel. The Vols made a quarterback switch halfway through the season, benching highly-touted true freshman Faizon Brandon in favor of George MacIntyre. Both have been mixing in, with packages to use Brandon's legs. Neither quarterback has been great, and Tennessee has the fewest passing yards in the SEC this season. It lacks any explosiveness through the air. The Volunteers have been entirely relying on the running game. Running back DeSean Bishop has been terrific for the Vols all year. He has been a workhorse, leading the country with 230 carries through 10 games. Bishop has averaged over 5.0 yards per carry on all those touches, ranking top-10 in the country in yards and touchdowns. On the other side of the ball, it has been a lockdown defense leading the way for Tennessee. The Volunteers have allowed just 14.3 points per game this season, the fewest in the SEC. They rank top-10 at preventing explosives and top-five at creating Havoc. LSU might lead the country in sacks, but Tennessee ranks second, just one back. Ten players on the Vols' defense have multiple sacks this season, with Tyree Weathersby and Xavier Gilliam leading the way. The defense has been especially dominant against the pass. Tennessee has held opposing pass attacks to just 164.2 yards per game. Dejuan Lane and Ty Redmond are elite in this secondary, ashe Vols have surrendered just four passing touchdowns all season. This is a very interesting game to handicap. If you strip out all the noise and intangibles and just look at the matchup and teams on the field, you can make a case that LSU is the better team. It's more talented, ranks inside the top 11 nationally in Success Rate on offense and on defense (Tennessee ranks 40th and 34th), and most people would say it has the better coach. Nearly every trusted power rating system has LSU rated higher than Tennessee, including our Action Network Betting Power Ratings . But you can't ignore the intangibles. And something always seems to be off with LSU and with Lane Kiffin-coached teams. When it comes down to the small details, the Tigers have failed all season. They rank 103rd in the country in turnover margin, 52nd in penalties and 98th in red-zone conversion percentage. Three areas that have killed the Bayou Bengals this season. It hasn't always been pretty for Tennessee, especially on offense, but the defense has been nails. It has been absolutely dominant at home this season, allowing just 11.3 points per game at Neyland Stadium. Nobody has scored more than 20 points in Knoxville, and that includes matchups against three top-10 teams. Speaking of top-10 teams, Kiffin is now 6-19 in his career against top-10 opponents. He's 1-9 on the road against top-10 teams, with seven straight losses. He's already 0-3 against top-10 teams this season. I don't expect either offense to be overly successful in this matchup between two strong defenses. I wrote about how good Tennessee has been at home this season. But on the other side, defense often comes down to effort, motivation and give-a-damn. The Vols are certainly going to have a lot more of that. LSU is a team full of hired guns that Kiffin got out of the transfer portal for one season. Their season just ended last week. Do they care about this game? We saw the way Leavitt responded when asked about skipping the Alma Mater after last week's loss. He doesn't care about Louisiana State University. He came here to try and win a national title, and that hope is now gone. Tennessee is playing at home in Neyland Stadium, knowing how its fans feel about Kiffin and how loud that place will be, with a playoff spot and SEC Championship berth on the line. Give me the motivated team with everything still in front of it over the team of hired mercenaries with nothing to play for. Pick: Tennessee ML (Play to -110)

Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud · LSU Tigers On SI Fri, November 20, 2026 at 9:58 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads LSU football had its playoff hopes ended last week with the last-minute loss to Texas. Now LSU travels to Tennessee , and what would've been a resume-strengthening game, has turned into a game that LSU can play spoiler in. Tennessee sits at 8-2 and ranked No. 9 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and a loss would tumble the Volunteers out of the running for a playoff spot. With LSU having no major post season games to play for, it's looking to play spoiler. A Top-10 Win When It's Over Nov 14, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; Louisiana State Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin reacts during the second quarter against the Texas Longhorns at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LSU wins 28 to Tennessee's 20. LSU was so close to taking down Texas, and even Alabama, but a few key mistakes prevented it from winning. LSU has shown it hasn't fixed those problems, especially in the red zone, if LSU does show up and fix those problems in any game, it wins. That's what holds LSU out of the playoffs. LSU ranks No. 1 in adjusted EPA/play, No. 10 in net yards, No. 8 in total offense, No. 5 in total defense, No. 13 in point differential and No. 8 in SRS, which is strength of schedule and point differential. LSU is a good team. But costly mistakes in the red zone, like six interceptions, will crush your chances to win. But if LSU shows up and has its issues fixed, it will be the better team in Neyland this weekend. If not, that's up in the air. LSU's Advantages Nov 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers wide receiver Jackson Harris (4) runs the ball during the second half against Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LSU's defense has been really good all season, but the offense leaving the defense in hard positions with bad field position and quick drives has left it reeling at points. But Tennessee has a problem coming to town: Jackson Harris. Harris has emerged as one of the best receivers in the country, just recently being named to the Biletnikoff semi-finalist list. Harris has been great inside, outside, short and deep for LSU, and has been a problem for defense after the catch and in the air. Tennessee cannot afford another slow defensive start, like its had sometimes this season, and Harris will torch the Vols. But Tennessee has to be the most careful at the line of scrimmage. LSU is home to a scary pass rush, and with Tennessee having some protection problems this season, the Tigers are ready to pounce on that. LSU is coming off of its most aggressive game yet, relentlessly pressuring Texas. LSU got after Arch Manning and forced three turnovers and a plethora of other broken plays and spoiled schemes. LSU needs to lean on its strengths to make the Vols uncomfortable. home.headline: George MacIntyre Gave His All to Tennessee Football on Saturday and it Showed
home.blurb: This goes to show that MacIntyre was battling the knee injury throughout the game. This is something that limited him in practice all week through the build-up, but it wasn't something that would keep him out of action. Many believed that he would be used in a limited role, and he was for the most part. On Saturday night, it seemed like it was more of Faizon Brandon's game than it was MacIntyre's. "Yeah, I just kind of always had the kind of fighter mindset that, you know, if I’m dressed out, then I’m ready to go. So, yeah, at the end of the day I was dressed out and ready, and, you know, I just thought, at a stage like this, it’s hard to pass up any opportunity to play. So I was going to be out there if I could," MacIntyre said. The Tennessee Volunteers have been in a weird situation, as they have been using two different quarterbacks. This includes George MacIntyre , who has started every game since the Arkansas game, except for the Saturday contest against the LSU Tigers. This was due to a knee injury that he suffered against the Texas A&M Aggies. However, he still found a way to play in this game, even when some believed he wouldn't make it on the field for the contest. Following the game, MacIntyre discussed how his knee was holding up . George MacIntyre Talks About His Knee Injury After the Game vs. LSU "It held up well during the game. Doesn’t feel the best right now, but, you know, we got a whole another week to recover and get ready for Vanderbilt," MacIntyre said. However, MacIntyre did everything that he could, and even put his health on the line to bring something new to the table. He finished the game with 79 passing yards on 12 completions. He also finished with a touchdown pass. George MacIntyre Credits His "Fighter Mindset" The question is, why would he want to do this? He was asked about it at the post-game press conference, and he credited his "fighter mindset". Even when he wasn't on the field, he was finding a way to be a good teammate to Brandon, which goes to show that his presence is needed even off the field, as he is in a split-quarterback system that isn't seen much across the country. MacIntyre even commented on Brandon's two touchdowns on the night. George MacIntyre Was a Great Teammate to Faizon Brandon "Yeah, it was great. Always there to support him. You know, when he’s doing well, the team’s doing well. When I’m doing well, the team’s doing well. So it was really great to see just anyone get in the end zone, really," MacIntyre said. With all of this being said, MacIntyre gave his all to Tennessee on Saturday night. He battled through an injury, made it a point to play, and was a teammate to his competition on the sideline. This is what it takes to make a difference on the road to what could be the second playoff appearance under head coach Josh Heupel. picks.headline: Game Preview as SMU Travels to Face No. 5 Notre Dame in Tough Road Test
picks.blurb: Game Preview as SMU Travels to Face No. 5 Notre Dame in Tough Road Test Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL SMU SPORTS NEWS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET SI.COM MUSTANGS FB MEN'S BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM MISTANGS BB DALLAS — The SMU Mustangs (7-3, 5-3 ACC) face one of their toughest road trips of the season this weekend. The Mustangs will travel to South Bend to face the No. 5 Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1) Saturday night at the historic Notre Dame Stadium. The Mustangs haven’t traveled to South Bend since the late 1980s. SMU holds a 1-6 record against the Fighting Irish on the road. Notre Dame leads the all-time series 10-3 overall. SMU faces a tall task after being routed in their first ACC loss at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in over three years. The Mustangs were drilled by No. 13 Wake Forest 49-7 last week. The Demon Deacons outgained SMU 535-275 while holding the Mustangs to 209 passing yards and 69 total rushing yards. As a result, SMU's chances of heading to Charlotte for the ACC championship game and a potential shot at the College Football Playoff have grown slimmer. SMU Head Football Coach Rhett Lashlee spoke during this week's media availability on his team’s performance last week and the challenge that this week presented to bounce back. “Life’s about opportunities, we had one last week we didn't take advantage of it. We have done a good job of taking advantage of our opportunities here. We did not put our best foot forward last week,” said Lashlee during Tuesday’s media availability. “Sometimes when that happens if we were playing someone that we were expected to beat or what not. I don’t know what you gain from that, but having the opportunity to go on the road against an elite opponent we know it's going to take our very best to beat regardless of what happened last week. I like that it's a great opportunity, a great challenge, and we get to see what we are made of and how we respond to that opportunity.” Notre Dame has been a top team in college football this season. After famously being left out of the College Football Playoff last season, Head Football Coach Marcus Freeman and his team have gone to work to ensure the Fighting Irish don’t leave any boxes unchecked for a guaranteed ticket to the postseason. The Irish are 9-1 through 10 games with a staple win over the ACC leader and former No. 1 team in the country, the Miami Hurricanes, atop their season resume. Notre Dame leads the nation in the fewest yards allowed to opposing offenses. While boasting one of the nation's best offenses. Junior quarterback C.J. Carr is top 10 in passing touchdowns this season with 23, while being among the top 25 in total passing yards with 2,385 this season. Carr has been in the Heisman conversation all season in his second season as a starter. He has only been intercepted twice and sacked three times this season. He is coming off a 200-yard performance against Boston College, after throwing for a season-high 319 yards against Miami. The second-year starter has a veteran pair of wide receivers bolstering the passing attack. Senior wide receiver Jordan Faison leads the receiver room with 615 yards on 49 catches with six scores. Not far behind him is junior receiver Micah Gilbert, who has recorded 614 yards on 38 grabs with six of his own scores this season. Fellow senior Jaden Greathouse is also a reliable weapon for Carr this year, securing 25 catches for 354 yards after dealing with injury for most of last season. The multiple weapons for the home team will be a massive test on the SMU’s secondary. Pick your champion (you can change it later). We’ll email you when brackets open. After losing both star running backs to the NFL, Notre Dame’s rushing attack has been bolstered by a pair of young stars with only 11 yards separating them. Freshman running back Jonaz Walton leads the team in rushing yards with 655 yards this season, averaging 7.0 yards per carry this season with five scores. The true freshman ran for over 140 yards and a score in Notre Dame’s 41-7 win over Boston College last week. Sophomore running back Nolan James Jr. is second on the team in rushing yards with 644. The second year back has had more than 120 attempts running the football this season, with a knack for finding the end zone. James Jr. has scored 10 times so far this season, the most on the roster. SMU allowed 286 rushing yards with 6.4 yards per carry against Wake Forest last week. The Mustangs will have one of the most talented backfield duos in the country rushing at them Saturday night. Lashlee went on to describe Notre Dame’s style of play as methodical and patient, yet still able to be explosive. “The way they play allows them to be patient, methodical, and just wear on you,” said Lashlee. “Because of their talent they create explosive plays, but they are not necessarily wired where they have to. They have no problem going on 10, 12, 13 play drives and just wearing on you. So that's what you worry about over the course of the game.” SMU gears up for one of its toughest tests of the season Saturday in a game that has been circled on the calendar since the schedule was released. NCAAF After one of the most disheartening losses of the college football season, my SMU vs. Notre Dame prediction expects the Mustangs to suffer another blowout loss to a Top 25 program. No. 6 Notre Dame is a 20.5-point home favorite over 7-3 SMU for Saturday's 7:30 p.m. ET (NBC) game at Notre Dame Stadium in Notre Dame, Ind., as my college football picks back Marcus Freeman's team to pour on style points against an SMU squad that allowed 42 first-half points against Wake Forest last week. Spread prediction: Notre Dame -20.5 Over/Under prediction: Over 55.5 TOP PICK Who will win SMU vs Notre Dame: Notre Dame -20.5 The College Football Playoff selection committee moved Notre Dame down a spot last week after the Fighting Irish won by 34 as a 30.5-point favorite. If Notre Dame wants to earn a top-four seed and a bye, it needs to blow SMU out and score some style points, especially after No. 11 Wake Forest beat the Mustangs 49-7 last week. With the extra motivation to help its CFP seeding, I like the Fighting Irish to cover up to -20.5 against an SMU team that's 0-2 ATS vs. Top 25 teams this season. The Mustangs' defensive issues have been clear in those games, with them allowing 45 points per game against ranked opponents. This Notre Dame offense is one of the most efficient in the country, sitting No. 1 nationally in available yards percentage (64.1%) and No. 7 in points per game (39.5). In eight games as a 20+-point favorite this season, Notre Dame is 5-3 ATS. SMU vs Notre Dame Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 Between Notre Dame's offensive efficiency and SMU's defense no-showing against quality opponents, I would play the Over at 57.5 or better . SMU has hit the Over in both its games against Top 25 teams this season, while allowing 41+ points in both games. Notre Dame's offense is fourth nationally in success rate (51.4%) and has scored 31+ in eight of 10 games this season. The Mustangs should do enough damage for the Over to hit, too. Kevin Jennings is top 10 in the country in both passing yards (2,973) and TD passes (26), and SMU likely only needs 20 points for the Over, a number they've reached in all but one game this season. SMU vs Notre Dame prop: Notre Dame team total Over 38.5 Notre Dame has been a machine against lesser opponents this year, which is why I like the Fighting Irish's team total Over up to 39.5 . CJ Carr is one of the best QBs in the country, sitting sixth in QBR (83.8), and he shouldn't struggle against an SMU defense that's 65th in EPA per dropback. And no team pays off quality drives as consistently as Notre Dame, with the Fighting Irish leading the country in points per opportunity (5.04) . Notre Dame is averaging 42.2 points per game in the eight games it's been favored by 20+ points. SMU vs Notre Dame combo SMU just took one of the most embarrassing losses of the season and now has to travel 1,000+ miles to take on a Fighting Irish team that could use some style points. There's a blowout brewing. Freeman's team hasn't messed around with lower-tier opponents this season, and SMU's one-dimensional offense will have trouble getting into a rhythm against a defense that's third nationally in available yards percentage (31.3%) and fourth in adjusted EPA per play. If SMU can't score to make up for its own defense, Notre Dame will run away with this quickly. No team has a higher net EPA per play in the country than the Irish, and they need to show the CFP selection committee they're a top-four team with a big win. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:39 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame blew out Boston College 41-7 … and it dropped a spot in the College Football Playoff rankings to No. 6. It doesn't matter – as long as the Irish win, they'll end up in the tournament. But drop a game over the last two weeks, and all CFP bets are off. SMU had its chance last week to all but land a spot in the ACC Championship, but one 49-7 rocking from Wake Forest later, and now it's looking to play spoiler to Notre Dame's season. Notre Dame vs SMU: Quick Hits SMU not only got blown out by Wake Forest, but that was the final home game. The Mustangs close out at Stanford. Notre Dame still has to deal with a road game at Syracuse to close things out. These two haven't played since 1989 – a 59-6 Notre Dame win. The Irish are 10-3 in the series going back to 1930. How To Watch Notre Dame vs SMU Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame, IN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why SMU Will Win SMU is still a dangerous team, even after the disaster against the Demon Deacons. The offense is terrific, with a great pace and balance that can be impossible to stop when it gets into a rhythm. Notre Dame hasn't faced too many sharp passing teams, but there was a problem against the stronger quarterbacks. BYU's Bear Bachmeier hit 65% of his passes in the 28-24 win, and Miami's Darian Mensah almost pulled the game out of the fire, throwing for 269 yards and three scores. One loss, one close call, and those were the two times the Irish allowed more than 300 total yards. SMU has one of the nation's most efficient passing games for an offense that averages 456 yards per game. Why Notre Dame Will Win How did Wake Forest destroy SMU? It came out roaring, and it was over. The Demon Deacons cranked up the pass rush against a leaky SMU line, and the three takeaways made things ugly. Yes, SMU works with a pace, but when it doesn't work, everything fizzes. But it's about the takeaways. SMU is 2-3 when turning it over multiple times, with 14 turnovers packed into those five games, and with nine turnovers in the three road games. Notre Dame is sixth in the nation in takeaways with 20. Notre Dame vs SMU Prediction, Betting Lines Yes, the Mustangs have a fun offense, and the quick-hitting style will hit the Irish defense for a few scores to throw a scare into the fan base for a half, but CJ Carr and the Notre Dame passing game are pretty good, too. Between the turnovers and lots of penalties, SMU isn't perfect. A few good drives will stall with giveaways, and even though the pass rush will get to Carr on a few third downs, the Irish will be locked in. They'll take over and pull away in the second half. We have — and holy smokes that went quick. It feels like it was just yesterday when the Irish were in the land of cheese playing the role of football dachshunds, and now it's the middle of November, and the SMU Mustangs are coming to town for Notre Dame's senior day. I'm going to need some real cheering up at the thought of the sadness… Put down your Michelob and pick up some micheladas. I know… I know. While I still maintain burritos are king, I never once said tacos weren't also royalty. THREE OTHER GAMES It's kind of a weird two weeks left in college football, but for this week, here are the three other games I'm paying the most attention to on Saturday. Ohio State Buckeyes VS Nebraska Cornhuskers — NOON UCLA Bruins VS Michigan Wolverines — 3:30 PM South Carolina Gamecocks VS Georgia Bulldogs — 7:30 Ohio State has been left for dead by a lot of people, and yet… they're still in striking distance of the playoffs. Can UCLA make themselves for real — like really for real (even against a crap Michigan team)? The CFP committee loves South Carolina, will this game against Georgia in Columbia show us why? I've been back and forth with myself all week about this game. Either SMU shows up already defeated, or they show up ready to prove last week's embarrassment against Wake Forest was just a dumb moment in time. I'm at the point now where I don't think it matters. Notre Dame is a team that has everything it needs to win a national championship this season, and everything seems to be clicking on both sides of the ball — as they get healthier and healthier. Notre Dame 45, SMU 10

(IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Aiden Kauffman · Roundtable Sports Sat, November 21, 2026 at 10:37 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Slow starts have defined SMU's season, and Saturday night is the worst possible place to keep that habit alive. Notre Dame averages 23.8 points in the first half, second nationally. At home, that number climbs to 28.8, which leads the country. The Irish do not ease into games and they certainly will not do it in their final home appearance of the season with a College Football Playoff berth still in reach. READ MORE: How To Watch SMU At Notre Dame As Mustangs Aim For Stunning Upset The Mustangs have spent all year needing a quarter or two to find themselves. It worked often enough to produce a 7-3 record, but Wake Forest exposed the danger last week with 42 first-half points in a 49-7 rout at Ford Stadium. That formula will not work here. So what's the key to keeping it close against the 20-point favorite Irish? The encouraging part is that Notre Dame's early dominance comes with an exploitable detail. Despite all those first-half points, the Irish rank 98th nationally in first-half time of possession share at 48 percent. They score quickly rather than sustain long drives, which means the ball is available if SMU takes advantage. That is where all three phases matter. Offensively, Kevin Jennings has been excellent, ranking seventh nationally with 2,973 passing yards and fifth with 26 touchdowns. The issue has not been talent but rhythm. SMU's opening drives have too often ended in punts, turnovers or failed fourth downs that give opponents short fields. Scoring on the first possession would do more for the Mustangs' chances than any adjustment Rhett Lashlee makes at halftime. Defensively, the assignment is survival through the first 15 minutes. SMU ranks t-21th nationally with 2.8 sacks per game, led by Marques White, who has 8.5 sacks and 12 tackles for loss. White is among the ACC leaders in both categories. Getting to C.J. Carr early would force Notre Dame into longer fields than the ones it has been scoring from. Allowing a quick touchdown drive turns a crowd of 77,000 into a problem. Special teams might be the quietest factor and the most important one. Field position has decided too many SMU games this season and in an environment like this, a muffed return or a short punt in the opening quarter could end things before they start. READ MORE: SMU Can't Be Mentally 'Broken' Ahead Of Notre Dame Showdown l The history does not help. Notre Dame has not hosted SMU since 1989, when the Irish won 59-6. The all-time series stands 10-3 in Notre Dame's favor. None of that is unreasonable. Notre Dame is 9-1 and ranked sixth in the country, playing its final home game of the season in front of a senior class that will be honored beforehand. The Irish will be emotional and motivated,and this is a bad week to hope they come out flat. But SMU has the offensive firepower to hang around if the game stays close. The Mustangs have shown they can score in bunches once they get going. The challenge is making sure they do not wait until halftime to start. Kickoff is 6:30 p.m. CT on NBC.

picks.blurb: Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Report: Tarik Skubal joining Mets on record 9-year, $450M deal TRENDING NFL Week 11 Winners-Losers Tom Jackson dies Tarik Skubal to Mets College football winners/losers Wemby drops 50 ... again Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions (Angela Driskell, Irish Breakdown) Bryan Driskell · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame will look to build its College Football Playoff resume when it takes on the 7-3 SMU Mustangs. The Irish fell to 6th in the playoff rankings on Tuesday despite blowing out Boston College by a 41-7 score last weekend. Notre Dame doesn't have a ranked opponent left on the schedule, but the Mustangs will help improve the overall strength of schedule, should the Irish earn a win. Notre Dame makes the playoff if they win out, but a dominant win would be even more helpful. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET Networ k: NBC/Peacock Here are our staff predictions for the game: Prediction : Notre Dame 38, SMU 17 Some of the magnitude of this game was diminished when SMU lost to Wake Forest last weekend in a blowout (49-7). SMU is a much better football team than it showed against the Demon Deacons, and that game reminded me a lot of Notre Dame's loss to Miami in 2017. It was one of those games that just got away from them early, but make no mistake, SMU is a dangerous football team. Notre Dame will need to play at a high level, because I expect SMU to come out looking to make an early statement and bounce back from their bad loss last weekend. The key for Notre Dame will be coming out early and jumping all over the Mustangs. They will need to quickly take away SMU's confidence and not let their potent offense get into any kind of rhythm. That will require the defense to be turned loose and be allowed to attack quarterback Kevin Jennings . If they are allowed to do that, and if the DL handles business, they will force Jennings to make mistakes, and that's how Notre Dame rolls in this game. My prediction is based on SMU being able to make some plays early due to their impressive talent at wide receiver and the fact Jennings is a dangerous player. I expect the Irish defense to quickly get up to speed and slow SMU down over the final two quarters. On the other side of the ball, Notre Dame will look to establish the run game early and get Nolan James Jr . and Jonaz Walton to get going. They will look to soften the Mustangs up and that's when CJ Carr should get rolling and pick the Mustangs apart. If the offensive line handles business the Notre Dame offense should have a big day and the Irish should roll. If Carr gets going early the offense could be extremely difficult to stop in this matchup. Prediction : Notre Dame 41, SMU 13 This is the final of three major tests for the 6th ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish. SMU is coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest at home during their own Senior Day matchup, but don't let that fool you, this is still a talented team making the trip up north. But like a lot of their opponents for the 2026 season, this matchup is more about Notre Dame living up to its potential than it is about facing an opponent that's superior. As it was said best in Wednesday's show, Marcus Freeman needs to know 'what time it is' in college football. SMU is a quality opponent, but not good enough that simply winning the game will boost their resume all on its own. I expect the Fighting Irish offense to come out firing early. Quarterback CJ Carr will hit some big plays early. The biggest question, will Notre Dame keep their foot on the gas after jumping out to an early lead? I think they answer that to a degree, but Freeman needs to learn from the lessons he's experienced in the previous two seasons. I have the Irish winning by 28 on Senior Day. I'm picking Notre Dame to win convincingly against SMU, but this game is about more than simply adding another win to the schedule. With the College Football Playoff committee evaluating every result, the Irish need to make a statement and show that they belong among the nation's elite. Notre Dame cannot afford to play down to its competition or let SMU hang around into the second half. This is an opportunity to dominate on both sides of the football, establish the running game, stretch the field offensively, and demonstrate the kind of physical superiority that separates playoff contenders from everyone else. The Irish need to take care of business, but they also need to make it look impressive. SMU has enough offensive talent, particularly with quarterback Kevin Jennings , to make things interesting if Notre Dame allows it. However, coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest, the Mustangs are vulnerable, and Notre Dame needs to take full advantage. I want to see the Irish defense create turnovers, get after Jennings, and keep SMU from finding any offensive rhythm. More importantly, Notre Dame needs to keep its foot on the gas rather than become conservative with a comfortable lead. The committee won't just see another win but it will see how the Irish perform against an opponent they are expected to handle. This is a chance to deliver a dominant performance, build momentum, and send a message that Notre Dame is a legitimate national championship contender. Prediction : Notre Dame 52, SMU 13 Before last weekend, I was going to pick a closer game (something like 38-24), but a combination of both the SMU blowout loss to Wake Forest and Notre Dame's dominant win over Boston College made me reconsider. First, I was pleased that the Irish played the attacking style of defense against Boston College that we saw for the second half of 2025, early in 2026, and then again against Miami. I don't think SMU's offensive line can hold up against the Irish front-seven when they play aggressively. The Mustangs gave up three sacks and six tackles for loss to Wake Forest, and rank 96th in the country in sacks allowed in road games this season. Getting SMU behind the sticks is going to put the onus on Kevin Jennings to make plays. He is really talented, but has a penchant for putting the ball in danger and making a few of those "what is he doing" kind of plays per game. There's a reason that SMU ranks 118th in the country in turnover margin at -6, and Notre Dame ranks 2nd at +16. Also, whether its due to corruption, malice, or just plain incompetence, there are no guarantees for Notre Dame when it comes to the CFP Committee. Marcus Freeman knows that it's not enough to just win these final two games - the Irish need to be dominant if they want to secure a home playoff game. With Wake Forest having such a big win last weekend over SMU - in Dallas no less - I think that will force Freeman and the Irish to keep the pedal down more than would be typical on a Senior Day when the staff typically tries to get all seniors a couple snaps once the game is in hand. Notre Dame's offense should not have much trouble moving the ball against a Mustangs defense that was blitzed by the two best offenses it faced (giving up 488.5 YPG against ranked opponents), and I think the Irish send a message on the scoreboard. Prediction : Notre Dame 35, SMU 10 SMU is a rising program, no question, which was why I was definitely surprised to tune into the game in the second half on Saturday to see such a lopsided score against Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons hammered SMU, leaving them off the scoreboard in the first half and quickly lighting up the scoreboard. While the Mustangs can certainly compete with anybody and Saturday's score was definitely out of character with how their season has gone, I don't think Notre Dame will have much trouble with them, provided they get off to a good start and play disciplined football. It really feels like Mike Denbrock has found his groove, with a great mix of run-and-pass with CJ Carr and Notre Dame's three-headed monster in the backfield: Jonaz Walton , Nolan James Jr. and Aneyas Williams . Give me the Irish.

Their last meeting didn't go too well for the visiting Mustangs as the Irish won 59-6 and took their foot off the gas relatively early in the second half. This year, however, it's a different looking SMU team that travels up north. This program is two years removed from playing for the ACC title and making the first ever 12-team College Football Playoffs. They have talent littered all over the field and will look to play spoiler to Notre Dame's Senior Day and their College Football Playoff hopes. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET TV : NBC/Peacock Line : Notre Dame -20.5; O/U 56.5 Let's kick off our preview of this matchup with an overview look at the SMU Mustangs Record at SMU : 45-19 (5th season) SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee is in the midst of his fifth season at the helm. Like the coach he's facing this Saturday, Marcus Freeman , he has had a winning record in every season he's been the head coach. In 2023 and 2024, the Mustangs posted back to back 11-3 seasons, playing for the ACC title in 2024 and making the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately, they lost soundly on the road against Penn State but that didn't take away from the great season he had. Last year, expectations were at an all-time high for Lashlee and SMU and they entered as one of the favorites to win the league. Unfortunately, they ended their season at 9-4 and weren't able to handle business down the stretch to get back to the ACC title game. This year, SMU is looking similar to the 2025 version of themselves rather than the 2023 and 2024 versions, but a win over Notre Dame in South Bend could drastically change the outlook of their season. Lashlee has the talent to compete with some of the top teams in the country at certain spots, but he needs to put it all together to make it back to the CFP which likely won't happen this season. After going a combined 22-6 from 2023 through 2024, they're now 16-7 from the start of 2025 through Week 11 of this year's college football season. Quarterback Kevin Jennings returned for his final year at the helm. To a degree, it's understandable given the talent on the perimeter with players like Yamir Knight , Jalen Cooper , Yannick Smith , Jalen Hale , Theo Melin Ohrstrom and Randy Pittman Jr. requiring a lot of touches. Their defense has been the area of struggle this season, as it was last season. In many areas, Maurice Crum Jr ., a former Notre Dame captain at linebacker, has changed the outlook of the defense for the better. But they're a 'feast or famine' type of unit ranking 13th in the country in tackles for loss and 20th in the country in sacks but also ranking 110th in the country in passing touchdowns allowed and 128th in the country in red zone scoring allowed. This season, when they've faced offenses that can score, they've allowed 41 points to Louisville, 30 points to Syracuse and 49 points to Wake Forest. away.headline: Notre Dame loses Luke Talich for the remainder of the 2026 season after devastating Achilles injury during win over SMU
away.blurb: Notre Dame suffered another big injury blow against SMU. Star safety Luke Talich is out for the remainder of the 2026 CFB season. The 6-foot-4, 222-pound safety from Cody, Wyoming, arrived in South Bend as a preferred walk-on despite having several Power Four offers coming out of the 2023 class. He wasn't a highly touted recruit coming out of high school as he should have been, but he steadily worked his way up the depth chart and earned a scholarship in the spring of 2024. The return of Brauntae Johnson helps, but it doesn't erase the loss Getting a player of his caliber back is enormous. Johnson was expected to be one of the leaders of this defense entering the season, and his return gives the Irish another experienced option at safety. Notre Dame now has to figure out how to replace a player who had become an important piece of its defensive identity. Starter Adon Shuler and Joey O'Brien are among the options available, but losing Talich's production, experience, and versatility changes the complexion of the position group. Johnson's return helps soften the blow. It doesn't make losing Talich any less significant. The recovery process typically involves surgery, immobilization, progressive weight-bearing, extensive rehabilitation, and eventually a return to football-specific activities. Potential return to football activities and competition Unfortunately, the timing makes it difficult to envision Talich being ready for the beginning of the 2027 season. A return at some point during that season is possible, but Notre Dame and Talich will have to be patient with the recovery. Talich has an additional year of eligibility available under the NCAA's five-for-five eligibility structure. That means he could potentially return to Notre Dame for the 2027 season if he decides that is the best path forward. It creates a fascinating decision. Does Talich enter the draft and bet on the evaluation he built throughout his senior season? Or does he return to Notre Dame, complete his rehabilitation and give NFL teams another opportunity to evaluate him at full strength? away.headline: Luke Talich and Leonard Moore injuries vs SMU give Notre Dame a terrifying problem
away.blurb: While the Notre Dame defense regrouped after allowing a 70-yard run to SMU on the Mustangs’ opening drive, it’s possible one of the plays that kept the Ponies out of the end zone also means Luke Talich is out of the game. It looks unlikely that Talich will be able to return for the rest of Saturday night’s game, but the bigger worry is that this could be serious enough to keep him out much longer than one week. Talich entered the game with three interceptions this season, according to Notre Dame's official football statistics , making a potentially extended absence an even bigger concern. As NBC showed Moore heading into the locker room with the trainers, the network also reported that Talich has officially been ruled out for the rest of the game. True freshman Joey O'Brien replaced him. Update : Both players are back on the sideline, however Talich came out on crutches and a boot. Moore ran back to the sideline out of the tunnel. It appears that the defensive back will get back in the game at some point, if not the next defensive possession. Brauntae Johnson’s return could unlock Notre Dame’s nastiest CFP secondary Luke Talich suffers apparent ankle injury during Notre Dame football game against SMU Talich went to defend a pass in the end zone and successfully broke it up, making sure the receiver didn’t come down with a touchdown catch. However, after the play, the safety stayed on the ground and waved teammates away when they came to help him up. At first, it appeared to be more about Talich needing a minute, as he looked to be testing his right ankle. Unfortunately, Notre Dame’s trainers eventually had to come onto the field and help him to the locker room, as he appeared unable to put any weight on the injured foot or ankle. Leonard Moore adds another Notre Dame football injury scare against SMU But wait, there’s more. On Notre Dame’s very next defensive possession, defensive back Leonard Moore had to leave the game after taking a shot to his left shoulder. As he walked off the field, it appeared he couldn’t, or didn’t want to, move his left arm much. Both Talich and Moore have been banged up plenty this season, and Notre Dame’s secondary has already had to deal with significant injury concerns . If one or both miss a significant amount of time, it would be an absolute disaster for the Fighting Irish as they push toward a potential College Football Playoff berth. away.blurb: SMU might be having an up-and-down season, but that doesn’t mean the Mustangs' offense isn’t one to be reckoned with. That’s one reason Notre Dame is so excited about the possibility of getting safety Brauntae Johnson back this week. It’s also why the news that defensive tackle Francis Brewu is officially off the availability report is big: it means he’ll be available to play Saturday night. Brewu, who has missed the last two games due to injury, has been an impact player since arriving in South Bend via the transfer portal from Pittsburgh. The 6-foot-1, 285-pound junior was removed from Thursday’s availability update after being listed as questionable Monday. He suffered the knee injury on October 31 against Navy, leaving that game after just a handful of snaps. Another defensive lineman for Notre Dame also has a chance to make his season debut. Sophomore Christopher Burgess Jr. was removed from Thursday’s availability report after previously being listed as out with a left tibia injury suffered before preseason camp. Like Brauntae Johnson, there’s a question about whether Burgess will actually play, given how long he’s been out. When defensive coordinator Chris Ash talked about Johnson earlier this week , he made it clear that the missed time could mean the safety won’t make the SMU game and would instead be ready later in the season. It’s a safe assumption that Burgess could face a similar challenge. Johnson, sophomore left tackle Will Black (concussion) and sixth-year defensive lineman Jason Onye (right knee) all remain questionable. Onye is another player who has missed significant time this year , and the fact that there’s even a chance he could get on the field against SMU is a good sign, especially with the College Football Playoff kicking off next month and the Irish still fighting for a berth. home.headline: Francis Brewu return gives Notre Dame a huge barrier for SMU's explosive offense
home.blurb: SMU might be having an up-and-down season, but that doesn’t mean the Mustangs' offense isn’t one to be reckoned with. That’s one reason Notre Dame is so excited about the possibility of getting safety Brauntae Johnson back this week. It’s also why the news that defensive tackle Francis Brewu is officially off the availability report is big: it means he’ll be available to play Saturday night. Brewu, who has missed the last two games due to injury, has been an impact player since arriving in South Bend via the transfer portal from Pittsburgh. The 6-foot-1, 285-pound junior was removed from Thursday’s availability update after being listed as questionable Monday. He suffered the knee injury on October 31 against Navy, leaving that game after just a handful of snaps. Another defensive lineman for Notre Dame also has a chance to make his season debut. Sophomore Christopher Burgess Jr. was removed from Thursday’s availability report after previously being listed as out with a left tibia injury suffered before preseason camp. Like Brauntae Johnson, there’s a question about whether Burgess will actually play, given how long he’s been out. When defensive coordinator Chris Ash talked about Johnson earlier this week , he made it clear that the missed time could mean the safety won’t make the SMU game and would instead be ready later in the season. It’s a safe assumption that Burgess could face a similar challenge. Johnson, sophomore left tackle Will Black (concussion) and sixth-year defensive lineman Jason Onye (right knee) all remain questionable. Onye is another player who has missed significant time this year , and the fact that there’s even a chance he could get on the field against SMU is a good sign, especially with the College Football Playoff kicking off next month and the Irish still fighting for a berth. picks.blurb: Kentucky at Missouri: Final thoughts, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Report: Tarik Skubal joining Mets on record 9-year, $450M deal TRENDING NFL Week 11 Winners-Losers Tom Jackson dies Tarik Skubal to Mets College football winners/losers Wemby drops 50 ... again Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at Missouri: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Sat, November 21, 2026 at 5:31 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football is facing their final road trip of the season as they travel to CoMo to face off against the Missouri Tigers . We have previewed the explosive Missouri offense and the Tigers' defense that has playmakers at every level. We also detailed the path to victory for the Wildcats to end this two game skid. This is an incredibly intriguing matchup as these are very similar teams in terms of talent and features two teams that have their backs against the wall following back-to-back losses. As we mentioned this week, Kentucky's offensive line is truly the key to this football team and a unit that has to get back to playing at a high level. This offensive line was rewarded for their play that led the Cats to a 7-1 start, which allowed them to be listed as semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. Over the last two weeks and specifically last week against Florida, they have not lived up to those honors. If Kentucky continues to play like that up front, they are in a very realistic danger of closing out the season on a four game losing streak. The offensive line was the position group Will Stein and his staff invested the most in overall for year one of this new regime, and it is fair to say by doing so they sacrificed other position groups like wide receiver. Kentucky needs the offensive line to be the best position group on the football field, and through eight weeks of the season they were consistently doing so. Expect an incredible effort from this group on Saturday night, they need to give Kenny Minchey time in the pocket and create displacement in the run game. This is where the game is won and lost as we saw last week against the Gators. Another key area is turnovers, which is an area that Kentucky was thriving in through the first eight weeks of the season. Over the last two weeks, the Wildcats have forced zero turnovers on defense and it has led to them being -4 in the turnover margin in those two losses. Slot corner Aaron Gates dropped an interception against Florida that could have swung the momentum of the game. Luckily, they could have those similar opportunities arise against Missouri. Per Clark Brooks, who does his own charting of all SEC teams on secstatcat.com, Austin Simmons has thrown the most passes this season that could have been intercepted. Simmons has faced good turnover luck, as he has just three interceptions on the season. If you look at the trend of Kentucky's wins versus losses in conference matchups, the Wildcats are facing well over 30 pass attempts per games in their five wins while facing just 20 pass attempts per game in their three losses. This could play out in the Wildcats favor, Missouri puts the ball in the hands of their quarterback as Simmons is averaging 30 pass attempts per game on the season. This game will fall on three areas in my opinion: which team wins the line of scrimmage, which team can create turnovers and which team simply wants the win more. This is a true coin flip game, Missouri is much more talented than their record shows. The Tigers had to face a Mississippi State team on the road against a healthy Kamario Taylor, an Ole Miss team that had superstar running back Kewan Lacy and just suffered back-to-back losses to Texas and Georgia. I have had a hard time deciding who wins this game because I really think these teams matchup evenly, but I ultimately think Missouri gets the win at home in an extremely hard fought game. Prediction: Missouri 31, Kentucky 28 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at Missouri: Final thoughts, prediction

picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Report: Tarik Skubal joining Mets on record 9-year, $450M deal TRENDING NFL Week 11 Winners-Losers Tom Jackson dies Tarik Skubal to Mets College football winners/losers Wemby drops 50 ... again Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction Dylan Ballard · SB Nation Mon, November 16, 2026 at 11:05 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That's a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn't sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there's still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein's first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers' playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it "not a good plan offensively or defensively," and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. Missouri 2026 Results W 54-14 vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff W 38-21 vs. Kansas W 27-17 vs. Troy L 31-24 at Mississippi State W 45-17 vs. Florida W 27-6 vs. Texas A&M L 31-3 at Ole Miss W 34-10 at Arkansas L 34-20 vs. Texas L 48-21 at Georgia Players to Know QB Austin Simmons: He won the job over Matt Zollers in the spring and opened the season 17 of 19 for 252 yards and four touchdowns. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky's run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons' favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can't set the edge, it's going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky's offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won't win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri's weak spot all year. Georgia's Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky's big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team's attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. It won't be pretty, but the Cats grind out a road win and stay alive for a 10-win season.

picks.headline: How No. 16 Kentucky football and Missouri match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.8% completions, 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had a challenging game in UK’s 21-14 upset loss to visiting Florida last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound product of Hendersonville, Tennessee, completed only 15 of 26 passes for 181 yards with one touchdown. In going 0-2 since returning from an Oct. 31 open week, Kentucky has allowed too much pressure on its QB. Minchey has been sacked six times and hurried 10 times total in losses to Tennessee and Florida. • Missouri’s Austin Simmons (62.3% completions, 2,379 yards, 21 touchdowns vs. three interceptions) has thrown for seven combined touchdowns in Mizzou’s past three games. A 6-4, 220-pound product of Miami, Simmons has already started a game vs. UK. Playing last season for Ole Miss, Simmons made his first career road start at Kroger Field. The QB threw two early picks as Ole Miss fell behind 10-0. Simmons steadied, however, and threw for 235 yards and ran for 44 yards and a TD as the Rebels rallied to beat Kentucky 30-23. Advantage : Missouri Running backs • UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (562 yards, 5.3 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the loss vs. Florida but had a hard time on the ground vs. the Gators. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, rushed 8 times for 21 yards vs. his home-state school. Since missing the Oklahoma game due to injury, Baxter has subsequently carried 20 times for 78 yards in the three games. Third-year player Jason Patterson (495 yards, 6 yards a carry, three TDs) had 22 yards on five rushes vs. Florida and caught a pass for nine yards. • Missouri’s Jamal Roberts (1,133 yards, 5 yards a carry, nine touchdowns) is second in the SEC in rushing. A 6-foot, 216-pound St. Louis product, Roberts has run for 100 yards or more in five games this season, and has gone above 200 yards rushing in a game twice. Ahmad Hardy led the SEC in rushing in 2025, running for 1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns. However, the 5-10, 210-pound product of Oma, Mississippi, missed the first seven games this season as he recovered from being shot in the left leg May 10 while attending an outdoor concert in Laurel, Mississippi. Since returning three games ago, Hardy has carried 10 times for 41 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (49 catches, 601 yards, three touchdowns) needs two catches and 29 receiving yards to shatter Barion Brown’s UK freshman marks (50 receptions, 628 receiving yards in 2022) for most catches and receiving yards in a season. Second-year player DJ Miller (26, 324, 1) caught four passes for 80 yards vs. Florida but also had a costly drop on UK’s final offensive possession of the game. • Missouri’s Cayden Lee is second in the SEC in receptions and first in the conference in receiving yards (879). A transfer from Ole Miss, the 5-11, 180-pound fourth-year player has caught at least five passes in every Mizzou game in 2026 other than last week’s 48-21 loss at No. 1 Georgia, when he was held to three receptions for 44 yards. Lee caught one pass for eight yards for Ole Miss in its win at Kentucky last season. Sophomore Donovan Olugbode is also having a big year for Missouri. The 6-2, 210-pound Chicago product has made 47 catches for 691 yards and eight touchdowns. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is tied for fifth in the FBS in receptions by a tight end with 50. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School has turned those team-high 50 receptions into 467 receiving yards and three touchdowns. A model of consistency, Rodriguez has caught either five or six passes in each of UK’s past six games. • Missouri’s Brett Norfleet has 14 catches for 120 yards and two TDs. The 6-6, 255-pound fourth-year player caught one pass for seven yards in last week’s loss to Georgia. Jude James has averaged 10 yards a catch on his seven receptions. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • In the losses to Tennessee and Florida the past two weeks, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has seemed to struggle in pass protection. Of the 6-8, 329-pound Madison Central product, Will Stein said “We all know, I know, (I) think everybody on our team knows (Wood’s) talent level is as good as you’re going to find in the country. It’s just consistency at that position.” • Missouri left tackle Cayden Green is the pillar of a Tigers offensive front that has surrendered the fewest QB sacks (nine) in the SEC. After starting five times for Oklahoma in 2023, Green transferred to Mizzou and started all 13 games in 2024 at left guard. Since switching to left tackle prior to the 2025 season, the 6-5, 324-pound Green has become a standout. So far in 2026, he has not allowed a sack or quarterback hit. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (36 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) had a streak of three straight games with at least one sack snapped vs. Florida. Tackle Tavion Gadson (33 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) also made four stops against the Gators. Gadson has now gone three games without a sack. • Missouri defensive end Daeden Hopkins is fourth in the SEC with seven sacks. The 6-6, 250-pound second-year player has also been credited with 11 quarterback hurries. A transfer from Miami, second-year tackle Donta Simpson has emerged as a disruptor for Eli Drinkwitz and Co. The 6-4, 300-pound Simpson has six QB sacks, 7.5 tackles for loss and eight QB hurries. Advantage : Even • Even though Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey (13 tackles) and WLB Bo Barnes (nine stops) were UK’s two leading tacklers vs. Florida, the prevailing thought was that UF’s ample success with the QB run game owed, in some part, to the Wildcats’ linebackers not fitting the run properly. “There were some big, big missed tackles in the game that sprung explosive runs by their quarterback,” Will Stein said. “That goes back to us not executing the fundamentals and technique of our position.” • Missouri WLB Nicholas Rodriguez leads the SEC in tackles with 107. The 6-foot, 225-pound Miami product has made at least 11 tackles in eight of Mizzou’s 10 games to date. MLB Robert Woodyard Jr ., a transfer from Auburn, is 22nd in the SEC with 64 tackles and has forced two fumbles and picked off a pass. Defensive backs • Kentucky safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant are tied for second in the SEC in interceptions with four apiece. However, neither has a pick in either of UK’s past two games, the losses at Tennessee and to Florida. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound product of Orlando, is ninth in the SEC with 76 tackles. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Lexington native, is 12th in the SEC with 74 stops. • Missouri cornerbacks Sione Laulea and Chris Graves Jr. are tied for second in the SEC with 10 passes successfully defended. Strong safety Santana Banner has recovered two fumbles and broken up six passes. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. For the second time this season, UK switched punters vs. Florida. After Wilson Berry punted for four games (averaging 42.6 yards a kick), UK went back to its original starting punter of 2026, Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara , vs. the Gators. O’Hara kicked three times vs. UF and averaged 46.3 yards a kick. On the season, O’Hara, an Australian, has averaged 41.5 yards on 20 punts. • Missouri place-kicker Blake Craig has missed nine of his 24 field-goal tries this season but has a long make of 53 yards. Craig has been better from outside 50 yards (5 of 7, 71.4%) than from inside 50 yards (10 of 17, 58.8%). Punter Brunno Reus is averaging 44.47 yards a kick and has stopped 18 of 47 punts inside the opponent’s 20-yard line. Punt returner DaMarion Fowlkes averaged 10 yards a return and had a 68-yard TD vs. Troy. As a kickoff returner, Fowlkes is averaging 24.8 yards on 12 returns. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Stanford vs California Prediction 11/21/2026 Today's College Football Picks Chris Ruffolo Stanford Cardinal California Golden Bears California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley, CA Saturday, November 21, 2026 Ron Romanelli Big Al McMordie See the full rankings: Best College Football Handicappers Stanford Cardinal vs Cal Golden Bears Prediction I'm laying the points with Stanford against Cal in the Big Game. I know rivalry games can make records look meaningless, and the Golden Bears would love nothing more than to keep their neighbors out of a bowl game. But at some point, I have to back the team that's actually moving in the right direction. Stanford has won three of its last four, while Cal has lost four straight and looks completely out of answers under Tosh Lupoi. The Cardinal can become bowl eligible for the first time since 2018, and I think they're playing with the urgency to make that happen. What's changed for Stanford is that the offense finally has something it can lean on. Micah Ford has rushed for at least 145 yards in three of the last four games, and he's averaging 137.5 rushing yards since the win over Elon. He just ran for 149 yards and three touchdowns in a 40-22 victory at Virginia Tech. That's a big deal against a Cal defense allowing 186.2 rushing yards per game. Stanford hasn't been a great rushing team over the entire season, but Ford's recent form gives the Cardinal a way to control possessions instead of asking Davis Warren to do everything. Warren has quietly done a nice job protecting the football. He's thrown for 2,406 yards with 14 touchdowns and only three interceptions, despite ranking among the national leaders in pass attempts. Stanford is still converting just 31.7 percent of its third downs, so it's not as though every offensive problem has disappeared. But when you can get the running game going and avoid handing the opponent short fields, you give yourself a much better chance to win close games. That's been missing from this program for a while. Cal's offense is the bigger concern for me. The Bears are scoring just 20.4 points per game and averaging only 78.7 rushing yards. That's an awful lot of pressure on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, who's thrown 11 touchdowns against eight interceptions. Chase Hendricks has been productive with 65 catches, but defenses don't have to respect the run nearly enough. Cal managed seven points at Virginia last week, and that loss followed defeats to Wake Forest , SMU and NC State. Those four losses have come by at least three touchdowns apiece. That's not a team that's simply catching a few unlucky breaks. I won't pretend Stanford is some defensive powerhouse. The Cardinal allow 35.8 points and nearly 449 yards per game, numbers that give Cal a legitimate opportunity to move the ball. But Stanford forced three turnovers against Virginia Tech, with Charlie Eckhardt recording two interceptions and a forced fumble. That was the Cardinal's first road win since 2024, snapping a 15-game skid away from home. The defense doesn't suddenly become great because of one afternoon, but there are signs of improvement when the offense gives it a chance. The travel angle is another reason I don't mind the road favorite here. Stanford has been crushed on several cross-country trips since joining the ACC, but going from Palo Alto to Berkeley is hardly the same situation. Cal also returns home after three straight road games, so maybe getting back to its own building helps. They haven't played in Berkeley since October 17, so there's some uncertainty there. The Bears have won the last two Big Games played in Berkeley, and that matters in a rivalry. Stanford, though, took back the Axe with a 31-10 win last season. Now there's a bowl bid waiting on the other side of another rivalry victory, while Cal is already eliminated from postseason consideration. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: Stanford -2.5 Need More? Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/cal as Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable . The initial injury report for Saturday's Cal-Stanford game was released Wednesday night, and a number of key Cal players are listed. Strong is the Bears' second-leading receiver with 35 catches for 478 yards, while McKinley, who also missed last week's game, is the team's co-leader in sacks with three. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. Carter Stadium to move within one victory of bowl eligibility. The Horned Frogs get their first shot at that sixth win Saturday, Nov. 21, when undefeated No. 2 Utah comes to Fort Worth for the home finale. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. CT on FOX. The Horned Frogs enter at 5–5 overall and 3–4 in the Big 12. Utah is 10–0 and 7–0 in conference play. If TCU pulls off the upset Saturday, it’s bowl eligible. Otherwise, the Frogs will have one more chance on Thanksgiving at No. 12 Texas Tech. Both opponents held their spots in Tuesday’s College Football Playoff rankings. Utah needed a late touchdown to beat Arizona 40–39 in Tucson last week. Quarterback Devon Dampier accounted for four touchdowns and rushed for 100 yards, so the Frogs will have their hands full even when a play breaks down. TCU held Kansas State to 10 points and won the turnover battle 2–0, but the offense still managed just 99 rushing yards and allowed four sacks. As I wrote in my Kansas State report card , the Frogs still have work to do up front. Can the Horned Frogs protect the football, finish drives and give the home crowd something to celebrate?
