(Photo by Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) (Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) Delayna Zepeda · Dallas Morning News Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 2 Utah at TCU 8 p.m. Saturday at Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth TCU (5–5, 3–4 Big 12), Utah (10–0, 7–0) TCU defeated Utah on the road in 2024, 13-7 What's at stake? The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. TCU will need to sustain drives, limit mistakes and take advantage of its scoring opportunities if it hopes to pull off the upset. The Frogs showed they can do that with their 20-10 victory over Kansas State. When Kansas State has the ball Undefeated Utah has been one of the strongest teams in the Big 12 this season and is looking to secure a spot in the conference championship game. The Utes will be one of TCU's toughest defensive challenges yet. The Frogs will need to limit Utah's scoring opportunities and find ways to slow down its offense if they hope to keep the game competitive. Quarterback Devon Dampier has completed 66.5% of his passes for 2,257 yards, 22 touchdowns and eight interceptions this season. His ability to make plays through the air will put pressure on TCU's secondary. TCU's defense will need to create pressure, limit big plays and force Utah into difficult third-down situations. If the Frogs cannot slow down Dampier and the Utes' offense, it could be a long night for the defense. This will be one of the toughest games of the season for the Horned Frogs. TCU is coming off a big win over Kansas State and will be hungry to prove it can compete with one of the best teams in the country. While I expect the Frogs to put up a fight, they have struggled to perform consistently under pressure this season. Utah has remained undefeated for a reason, and its strength on both sides of the ball will make this a difficult matchup for TCU. I expect the Horned Frogs to compete early, but Utah's consistency will ultimately be too much to overcome. Texas Tech has the lead over BYU to join the Utes in the title game. And that might be the Red Raiders' only chance of making the playoff. The Utes lead the Big 12 in rushing defense, allowing just 98.9 yards per game, while TCU ranks last in the conference in rushing offense at 106.5 yards per game. Even with leading rusher Jeremy Payne returning from injury last week, TCU managed just 99 rushing yards against Kansas State. Here are four keys to a Utah victory. Play Tight Man Coverage and Bring Constant Pressure Utah needs to be aggressive defensively from the opening possession. TCU has allowed 28 sacks this season, and its offensive line has struggled in pass protection. The Utes should play tight man-to-man coverage, get physical with TCU's bigger receivers and tight ends at the line of scrimmage, and bring consistent pressure. There will be some risk involved, and TCU could connect on a few explosive plays. However, I believe the reward outweighs the risk. Utah has the defensive personnel to make life difficult for TCU's offense, and consistent pressure should create opportunities for sacks and interceptions. Run a Balanced Offense TCU has one of the better defenses in the Big 12, allowing just 304.4 total yards per game. However, Kansas and Arizona both found success moving the football against the Horned Frogs by maintaining a balanced attack. Kansas finished with 451 total yards, including 285 passing and 166 rushing. Arizona recorded 441 yards, with 313 passing and 128 rushing. Utah is averaging 223.6 rushing yards and 247.8 passing yards per game. The Utes have the ability to attack TCU both on the ground and through the air. Keeping the play-calling balanced and utilizing Devon Dampier's dual-threat ability should prevent TCU from focusing on stopping one aspect of Utah's offense. Hold On to the Football One of TCU's biggest defensive strengths is its ability to force fumbles. The Horned Frogs have forced 12 fumbles this season and recovered eight. Kylin Jackson and Koron Hayward have combined for seven forced fumbles alone. TCU's defenders are aggressive when attacking the football, particularly when runners are fighting for extra yards. Utah needs to make ball security a priority throughout the game. TCU's defense is good enough to keep this game competitive, and giving the Horned Frogs extra possessions could make things much more difficult than they need to be. Rattle TCU's New Starting Quarterback With Jaden Craig doubtful due to an ankle injury, TCU is expected to start Adam Schobel, who would be making his first career start. Schobel has attempted just one pass this season, and Utah needs to take advantage of that inexperience. The Utes should bring pressure early, disguise coverages, and force Schobel into difficult third-down situations. Utah cannot allow an inexperienced quarterback to get comfortable with easy completions and extended drives. If the Utes can shut down TCU's rushing attack and force Schobel to beat them through the air, I like Utah's chances of creating turnovers and controlling this game defensively. Final Score Prediction No. 2 Utah 34, TCU 7 TCU's defense will present some challenges, but I believe Utah has too many weapons offensively. The Utes should be able to shut down TCU's struggling rushing attack, put consistent pressure on its inexperienced quarterback, and control the game. Utah improves to 11-0 and secures its spot in the Big 12 Championship Game .
